source_text.docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolv: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must independently APPLY at least one of the reported mutants and run it -- accepting the reported pass counts is copying a claim, not validating one.

task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's regression test at test/mix/tasks/letflow.seed_test.exs. Read step-04-test-designer.json's result.summary for the two claimed mutants (Mutant A: omit idp_realm_id -- claimed 0/4 pass; Mutant B: disable idempotency fallback -- claimed 3/4 pass). Independently APPLY AT LEAST ONE of these two mutants yourself (in a throwaway git worktree, per the same technique TEST-DESIGNER used -- never mutate the main checkout in place unless you revert-and-verify per the source_text rule) and run the test file against it to reproduce the reported fail count. Also confirm the unmutated post-fix run is 100% green by running it yourself.
acceptance_criteria: Post-fix (unmutated) test run independently reproduced, real output quoted, 100% green
At least one mutant independently applied and run (not merely re-read from TEST-DESIGNER's report), fail count matches or discrepancy is reported
All 3 ISS-0276 acceptance criteria confirmed covered by the test file (read the test file directly)
If mutating in a real worktree: worktree removed after; if mutated in the main checkout: git status --porcelain lib/ test/ verified empty
PASS or FAIL with itemized issues if FAIL

result.summary:
Independently re-ran the unmutated test file: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.seed_test.exs` -> `Finished in 2.8 seconds` / `Result: 4 passed`, zero failures -- real output quoted, matches TEST-DESIGNER's claim.

Independently applied Mutant A (omit "idp_realm_id" from @attrs) myself, not merely re-read from TEST-DESIGNER's report. Used a throwaway git worktree (`git worktree add ../letflow-mutant-validate-wt HEAD`), reusing this checkout's deps/build via MIX_DEPS_PATH/MIX_BUILD_PATH to avoid a network fetch. Edited lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex in the worktree to drop the "idp_realm_id" key from @attrs, then ran the test file there. Measured result: `Result: 0/4 passed` / `Failed: 4 tests`, each failing with `** (Mix.Error) mix letflow.seed: FAILED -- create_tenant/1 rejected the seed attrs: [idp_realm_id: {"can't be blank", [validation: :required]}]` on the test's own `Seed.run([])` call. This exactly matches TEST-DESIGNER's claimed 0/4 pass for Mutant A -- no discrepancy.

Worktree removed after (`git worktree remove ../letflow-mutant-validate-wt --force`); main checkout was never mutated -- confirmed `git worktree list` shows only the main checkout afterward, and `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` in the main checkout is empty.

Read test/mix/tasks/letflow.seed_test.exs directly and confirmed all 3 ISS-0276 acceptance criteria are covered: AC1 ("AC1 -- run/1 creates the bpm-default tenant row" describe block asserts slug and idp_realm_id both "bpm-default"), AC2 ("AC2 -- resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 succeeds post-seed..." describe block: resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 returns {:ok, tenant}, plus a second test proving the tenant's Postgres schema and tables were actually provisioned/migrated via information_schema, not just a bare row), AC3 idempotency ("idempotency -- running the task twice" describe block: two Seed.run([]) calls both return :ok, exactly one row with idp_realm_id == "bpm-default" afterward, resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 still resolves). AC3's doc requirement is prose-only (README + moduledoc), correctly left untested per the spec and task.description.

No @tag :skip anywhere in the file. No "TODO: implement test" strings. Fixtures don't depend on shared hardcoded external state -- the fixed "bpm-default" slug/idp_realm_id is intentional (the fix's whole point per design), and setup/on_exit proactively delete any pre-existing bpm-default tenant + drop its schema both before and after each test, so a prior crashed run can't leave contaminating state. Tests are self-sufficient -- each test calls Seed.run([]) itself rather than depending on another test having run first; :async false plus real (non-sandboxed) Postgres via Sandbox.mode(:auto) is the same pattern already used elsewhere in this suite (test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_event_seed_test.exs) for this exact reason (a second real DB connection is required). No hardcoded secrets or connection strings.
